rule_catalog.title: Bronze adds only _ingested_at
rule_catalog.description: The bronze object is the staging object with `,_ingested_at` appended to record 1 (whatever it contains) and `,<timestamp>` appended to every other record, before that record's terminator. The BOM, every byte of every record, the record order, the terminators and the missing final newline are preserved. Blank and malformed records get the suffix too. A 0-byte staging object gives a 0-byte bronze object. Nothing is decoded, validated, altered or dropped in bronze

rule_catalog.title: Bronze round-trip self-test
rule_catalog.description: Pipeline self-test, not a file check: removing the last field (the final `,` and what follows it) from every bronze record reproduces the staging bytes exactly, with the same length and SHA-256. It runs on every load, before anything is published. A mismatch is a defect of our writer: the run fails, the file is not rejected, and the same bytes are retried after the fix

rule_catalog.title: Lineage manifest per file
rule_catalog.description: One write-once manifest per (dataset, SHA-256 of the staging bytes), at `_manifests/<dataset>/<sha256>.json`, written with `If-None-Match: *`. Fields: the verbatim source key, VersionId (null while versioning is off), size, ETag, SHA-256, staging LastModified, record count and data-row count, the header as received and `header_matches_registry` (information only, never a gate), `_ingested_at`, the `run_id` of the first ingest, `_rules_version`, and Decimal control totals computed from the raw strings with a count of cells that did not parse. It holds no scan status, no checksum comparison and no check hits. The source key is data: it is never interpolated into a path, query or command. If the manifest cannot be written, the run fails

rule_catalog.title: One timestamp per file, idempotent
rule_catalog.description: `_ingested_at` has one value per bronze object: UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, set at the first ingest of a given (dataset, SHA-256 of the staging bytes). Re-delivering bytes already ingested creates no new bronze object and no new timestamp. If those bytes are not the dataset's current snapshot, that snapshot becomes current again and the event is logged. VersionId is recorded and is never the idempotency key

rule_catalog.title: Line is valid UTF-8, no control chars
rule_catalog.description: The bytes of each data record decode as strict UTF-8 (the BOM is stripped from record 1 only) and contain no C0 control character U+0000–U+001F. The line terminator is not part of the record. A failing row is excluded with `UNDECODABLE_LINE` or `CONTROL_CHAR` and is evaluated by no other rule

rule_catalog.title: Empty records
rule_catalog.description: A data record whose fields are all zero-length (a blank line, `,`, `,,` and so on) is excluded with `EMPTY_RECORD` and is evaluated by no other rule. It is tested before SQ-01. Every empty record is a failure: none is "expected"

rule_catalog.title: Line has the registered field count
rule_catalog.description: Parse contract: UTF-8, BOM stripped, record 1 consumed as the header, fields split on every `,` with no quote handling and no trimming, columns assigned by position, numbers parsed from their strings as exact decimals and never as floats. CRLF or LF endings and a missing final newline are accepted. A data record that does not split into exactly 3 (`transactions`), 2 (`industry`) or 8 (`sm_spend`) fields is excluded with `FIELD_COUNT` and is evaluated by no other rule

rule_catalog.title: Customer ID valid and unique
rule_catalog.description: (a) `ID` matches G-INDUSTRY-ID and yields the integer `customer_id`; otherwise the row is excluded with `BAD_CUSTOMER_ID`. (b) The derived `customer_id` is unique among rows that pass (a); otherwise every copy is excluded with `DUPLICATE_CUSTOMER_ID`, identical copies included. The pipeline never picks a winner

rule_catalog.title: Industry outside the registered list
rule_catalog.description: On included rows, `Industria` is normalized to Unicode NFC and mapped to one of the 6 registered values and its code: Restaurantes `RESTAURANTS`, Producción `MANUFACTURING`, Retail `RETAIL`, Tecnología `TECHNOLOGY`, Servicios profesionales `PROFESSIONAL_SERVICES`, Salud `HEALTHCARE`. Any other value, an empty one included, keeps its row in silver with `industry_code` = `UNMAPPED`, `is_industry_unmapped` = true and the raw value kept; reason `UNMAPPED_INDUSTRY`. The codes are an inferred convention

rule_catalog.title: Customer-month key valid and unique
rule_catalog.description: (a) `ID` matches G-ID and yields `customer_id`; otherwise the row is excluded with `BAD_ID`. (b) (`customer_id`, month) is unique among rows whose `ID` and `month` both parse, whatever their amount; otherwise every copy is excluded with `DUPLICATE_KEY`

rule_catalog.title: Month is a month-end date
rule_catalog.description: `month` matches G-TX-MONTH (non-padded month/day/year), is a real calendar date and is the last day of its month. It is converted to `YYYY-MM`. A padded date (`01/31/2022`), another format or a day that is not month-end is excluded with `BAD_MONTH`. Validate with the pattern before any date parser, because `%m/%d/%Y` and `M/d/yyyy` parsers accept padding

rule_catalog.title: Amount is a plain decimal number
rule_catalog.description: `amount` matches G-AMOUNT; otherwise the row is excluded with `BAD_AMOUNT`. `1e3`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `+5`, `.5`, `5.`, `1,5`, an empty value and any space all fail. No NULL or 0 is ever substituted.

rule_catalog.title: Negative amount
rule_catalog.description: On included rows, an amount below 0 keeps its row in silver with `is_negative_amount` = true; it stays in every sum and is not a paying month; reason `NEGATIVE_AMOUNT`

rule_catalog.title: Missing customer-months
rule_catalog.description: The delivery is expected to be a dense panel. A finding `MISSING_CUSTOMER_MONTH` is recorded for each panel cell (U × W) that no source row carries. A cell whose rows were excluded is also a hole, but it is counted under the rule that excluded it, not here. Nothing is imputed, and both kinds of hole follow H1–H11

rule_catalog.title: Month valid and unique
rule_catalog.description: `Month` matches G-SM-MONTH; otherwise the line is excluded with `BAD_MONTH`. A `Month` repeated among lines that pass the pattern excludes every copy with `DUPLICATE_MONTH`.

rule_catalog.title: Missing months in the series
rule_catalog.description: A finding `MONTH_GAP` is recorded for each calendar month between the earliest and the latest included month that no source line carries. The month stays absent and is never zero-filled

rule_catalog.title: Spend cells match the $0.000 format
rule_catalog.description: Each of the 7 spend cells matches G-SPEND. The `$` is stripped and the sign is kept. If any cell fails, the whole month line is excluded with `BAD_SPEND_CELL`, and `failed_columns` lists the failing cells

rule_catalog.title: Customers with no Industry row
rule_catalog.description: A finding `NO_INDUSTRY_ROW` is recorded, against `industry`, for each `customer_id` in included Transactions rows that has no included Industry row. In silver that customer has `industry_code` = `UNKNOWN` and `is_industry_unknown` = true. No Transactions row is excluded, flagged or changed. An Industry customer with no Transactions row is kept and is not a finding

rule_catalog.title: Month covered by only one dataset
rule_catalog.description: The two money datasets are expected to cover the same months. A finding `MONTH_NOT_IN_DATASET` is recorded for each month that has at least one included row in one of them and none in the other, against the dataset that lacks it. In `month_control` that month's S&M ÷ revenue ratio and tripwire are NULL

rule_catalog.title: Value fits its registered precision
rule_catalog.description: Money is DECIMAL, never float: `amount` DECIMAL(12,6) → `amount_value` DECIMAL(18,2); spend DECIMAL(12,3) → `spend_value` DECIMAL(18,0). Nothing is rounded, truncated or widened. A Transactions row whose `amount`, after dropping trailing fractional zeros and leading integer zeros, needs more than 6 decimal places or more than 6 integer digits is excluded with `PRECISION`. For `sm_spend`, G-SPEND already limits a cell to 6 integer digits and 3 decimals, so the rule is evaluated there and cannot fail while that pattern stands

rule_catalog.title: Keys removed since the previous run
rule_catalog.description: Each delivery is treated as a full snapshot, and silver is rebuilt from it. It is compared with the previous succeeded run of the same dataset. Keys: a Transactions (`customer_id`, month), an Industry `customer_id`, an S&M month. A key is delivered when any source row carries it, included or excluded. A finding `REMOVED_KEY` is recorded for each key delivered in the previous run and not delivered now.

rule_catalog.title: Values restated since previous run
rule_catalog.description: Each delivery is treated as a full snapshot, and silver is rebuilt from it. It is compared with the previous succeeded run of the same dataset. Keys: a Transactions (`customer_id`, month), an Industry `customer_id`, an S&M month. A key is delivered when any source row carries it, included or excluded. An included row whose key was included in the previous run with a different typed value (the amount; the NFC `Industria`; any spend cell) stays in silver with `is_restated` = true, reason `RESTATED_VALUE`, and its old and new values go to the restatement log. On a dataset's first run both parts have evaluated = 0 and status `na`

rule_catalog.title: Bronze rows = silver + excluded
rule_catalog.description: Exact, per dataset, on every run. (1) Data rows in bronze = included rows + excluded rows; each data row is in exactly one of the two; each excluded row has at least one failed exclude rule; each flagged row is included. (2) Silver `transactions` rows = included rows; silver `industry` rows = included rows; silver `sm_spend` rows = 7 × included lines. (3) In exact Decimal: Σ `amount` in silver = Σ of the included rows' source strings, recomputed independently from bronze; the same for Σ spend; Σ `amount_value` = Σ `amount` × 10,000; Σ `spend_value` = Σ spend × 100,000,000. (4) Lifecycle panel rows = U × W cells = included Transactions rows + holes. Control totals come from bronze and the manifest, never from documentation. Any break fails the run

rule_catalog.title: Lineage on every row
rule_catalog.description: Every silver row and every DQ-store record carries `_run_id`, `_source_key`, `_source_sha256`, `_ingested_at`, `_rules_version` (a hash of the rules config, which includes the catalog in this file) and `as_of_month`. Row-grain tables and DQ row records also carry `_source_line`. A row built from two sources (silver `customer`) traces to both through the run manifest. A row without lineage fails the run. The gold part of this rule is deferred

rule_catalog.title: Full rebuild, atomic publish
rule_catalog.description: Every run rebuilds silver and the DQ store in full, under a new run id, from the current bronze snapshot of each dataset. No file-level acceptance exists: every delivered file is loaded. The run is published atomically, only after every run control passes, and its pointer (`dq/latest.json` for the DQ store) is written last. A failed run publishes nothing and the previous publish stays live. Published runs are immutable. The summaries of at least the 24 most recent succeeded runs are retained for the trend. The gold part and the month-close retention of this rule are deferred

rule_catalog.title: Access and HR-sensitive masking
rule_catalog.description: (1) Customer-level data (silver and the DQ store) is Confidential-Financial pseudonymised data, readable only by the `finance`, `revops` and `data` roles. (2) `Team`, `PayrollExpenses` and `Freelance` are HR-sensitive: only `finance` reads their values; every other role receives `__restricted__`. The full policy is § Access and is part of this rule. The run asserts that HR-sensitive values appear in no log line, run report or `reason` string, and that silver `sm_spend` rows of those categories sit only in the `hr_sensitive` partition. Parts (3)–(5) of the original rule (suppression in shared aggregates) are deferred with gold

rule_catalog.title: Revenue × 10,000 (owner definition)
rule_catalog.description: `amount_value` = `amount` × 10,000 for every included row, in exact decimal arithmetic. The run asserts that `amount_value` ÷ 10,000 = `amount` exactly on every row

rule_catalog.title: S&M × 100,000,000 (owner definition)
rule_catalog.description: `spend_value` = spend × 100,000,000 for every included cell, in exact decimal arithmetic, with the sign kept. The run asserts that every `spend_value` is an integer and that `spend_value` ÷ 100,000,000 = spend exactly

rule_catalog.title: Paying means amount above zero
rule_catalog.description: `is_paying` = (`amount` > 0) on every included row. A zero or negative month is unpaid. A hole has `is_paying` NULL (H1). The run asserts the identity on every included row

rule_catalog.title: Cohort and left-censoring
rule_catalog.description: `cohort_month` is the customer's first known-paid month. `first_payment_ratio` = first paid amount ÷ next paid amount, where the next is the second known-paid month at any distance (NULL with a single payment). `first_payment_multiple` j is the integer in {2, 3} with abs(first − j × next) ≤ 0.05 × j × next, else NULL. `implied_start_month` = `cohort_month` − (j − 1) months, NULL when j is NULL. `cohort_censoring` is, in this order: `left` when `cohort_month` is the first month of W; `unknown` under H5; `probable_left` when `implied_start_month` ≤ the first month of W; `none` otherwise. Only `none` is a new logo. A finding `COHORT_UNKNOWN` is recorded for each customer with `unknown`

rule_catalog.title: Churn after 3 unpaid months
rule_catalog.description: A churn spell is an unsettled clean stretch of at least 3 unpaid months after the first known-paid month: internal (ended by a payment that does not settle it) or trailing (still open at `as_of_month`). Its months are `churned`, and `is_churn_event` marks its first unpaid month. A clean trailing stretch of 1–2 unpaid months is `grace`. A settlement found later restates the spell as a settled gap. Churn counts for months after `churn_confirmed_through` are NULL, never 0. The threshold 3 is a versioned parameter. An included row inside a broken stretch has state `unknown` (H3) and is flagged `STATE_UNKNOWN`

rule_catalog.title: Settled gaps: arrears, prepay, split
rule_catalog.description: A gap is a clean internal stretch of k ≥ 1 unpaid months between known-paid months p and q. x_m is the native amount of month m, and p−1 is the calendar month before p. "a ≈ b" means abs(a − b) ≤ 0.05 × b. The tests run in this order and the first match settles the gap: (1) arrears: x_q ≈ (k+1) × x_p; (2) prepay: x_{p−1} > 0, x_p ≈ (k+1) × x_{p−1} and x_q ≈ x_{p−1}; (3) split: x_{p−1} > 0 and x_p + x_q ≈ (k+2) × x_{p−1}. When p−1 is before W, tests 2 and 3 do not match. A settled gap gets `settlement_type` (`arrears`, `prepay`, `split`) and `settlement_confidence` (`high` for arrears and prepay, `low` for split) on its unpaid months and on its settling months: q for arrears, p for prepay, p and q for split. Its unpaid months have state `settled_gap`. `is_catch_up` marks q of an arrears gap and `is_prepaid` marks p of a prepaid gap. Amounts are never restated. The tolerance 0.05 is a versioned parameter. A finding `SETTLEMENT_HOLE` is recorded for each gap with `settlement_hole_affected` (H6)

rule_catalog.title: Reactivation versus pause
rule_catalog.description: The first known-paid month that ends an internal churn spell is `reactivated`: never a new logo, and the customer keeps its cohort. An unsettled clean internal stretch of 1–2 unpaid months is `paused`, and the payment that ends it is `paying`, not a reactivation. A known-paid month that ends a broken internal stretch is `paying` (H4) and is flagged `REACTIVATION_UNKNOWN`

rule_catalog.title: Outlier customers
rule_catalog.description: `is_outlier_customer` is true when the customer has at least 3 known-paid amounts and the median of them is ≥ 25 × the portfolio median, taken over all known-paid customer-months up to `as_of_month`. A median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. 25 and 3 are versioned parameters. An owner may add or remove a customer through a recorded statement in versioned config (`outlier_source` = `owner`, otherwise `rule`). Outliers are never removed from silver. A change in the flagged set from the previous published run is written to the restatement log. A finding `OUTLIER_INCOMPLETE_HISTORY` is recorded for each customer with `has_excluded_months` (H8). Publishing averages all-in and ex-outlier is deferred with gold

rule_catalog.title: Industry fixed per customer
rule_catalog.description: A customer has one industry (SCD type 1), applied to its whole history: silver `customer` holds exactly one `industry_code` per `customer_id`. The run asserts it

rule_catalog.title: Negative spend
rule_catalog.description: Spend keeps its sign as received. It is never made absolute, clipped, floored or reclassified. A negative cell has `is_negative_spend` = true, and its line is flagged with `NEGATIVE_SPEND` and the negative columns in `failed_columns` (`NEGATIVE_SPEND_OTHER_CATEGORY` when any of them is not `PayrollExpenses`, which also alerts Finance and Data). Its nature is unconfirmed: an adjustment and a budget plug are both possible. The monthly total in `month_control` is the exact sum of the 7 categories, negatives included

rule_catalog.title: Uneven split of a two-month total
rule_catalog.description: Two consecutive months m and m+1 of one customer are an uneven split when, with x the native `amount` and b = x_{m−1}: (1) months m−1, m, m+1 and m+2 are all known-paid (`amount` > 0), so the four-month window holds no hole and no unpaid month; (2) none of the four months has a `settlement_type`, whether from SB-06 or from an uneven split already tagged; (3) x_{m+2} = b; (4) x_m ≠ b; (5) x_m + x_{m+1} = 2 × b. Every test is an exact Decimal equality with no tolerance. This is not a versioned parameter: `amount_normalized` = b below is exact only because the sum is exact. Windows are tested from the earliest m upward, and a tagged month is never re-tagged. Both months get `settlement_type` = `uneven_split`, `settlement_confidence` = `high`, `amount_normalized` = b (which equals (x_m + x_{m+1}) ÷ 2 exactly) and the new column `uneven_split_start_month` = m as `YYYY-MM` (NULL on every other panel row). `is_catch_up` and `is_prepaid` stay false, and `lifecycle_state` stays `paying`. Both included rows are flagged with `failed_columns` [`amount`] and reason `UNEVEN_SPLIT: <m> and <m+1> sum to twice the amount of <m−1> and <m+2>`. Nothing else changes: `amount`, `amount_value`, `is_paying`, revenue totals, medians, first paid amounts, lifecycle states and the `gap` table. A pair is decided only once month m+2 is delivered, so a later delivery can tag it retroactively (CTO-10). Runs of 3 or more months and pairs whose two baselines differ are not covered (deferred, Q17)

rule_catalog.title: One lifecycle state per customer-month
rule_catalog.description: Every panel cell (U × W) has exactly one `lifecycle_state`: `pre_acquisition` (a month of a clean leading stretch); `new` (the first known-paid month of a customer whose `cohort_censoring` is `none`); `paying` (any other known-paid month that is not `reactivated`); `reactivated`; `settled_gap`; `paused`; `churned`; `grace`; `unknown` (H3). `is_provisional` is true on every row from the customer's last known-paid month through `as_of_month`. A cell with no state or more than one fails the run

rule_catalog.title: Unit tripwire: S&M ÷ revenue
rule_catalog.description: For each month with included rows in both money datasets, compare Σ `spend_value` (S) with Σ `amount_value` (R). The tripwire fires when R ≤ 0, S < 0.5 × R or S > 20 × R. The S&M line of that month is flagged with `UNIT_TRIPWIRE`, `month_control.is_unit_tripwire` = true, and Data and Finance are alerted. The fault may be in either dataset. The bounds [0.5, 20] are versioned parameters. `sm_to_revenue_ratio` = S ÷ R is stored as evidence

rule_catalog.title: Currency and basis are unconfirmed
rule_catalog.description: Silver `source_status` has exactly one row per money dataset, from versioned config: `currency_code` NULL, `currency_status` = `unconfirmed`, `revenue_basis_status` or `spend_basis_status` = `unconfirmed`, and `basis_hint` (`cash-like` for revenue, `budget-like` for spend). The values change only through a recorded owner answer. The run asserts the two rows exist with the configured values

rule_catalog.title: Scope of S&M vs revenue unconfirmed
rule_catalog.description: `scope_status` = `unconfirmed` on every `month_control` row, from versioned config, until a recorded owner answer says Transactions covers the customer base that the S&M spend acquires and serves. `sm_to_revenue_ratio` is evidence and never sets the status. The run asserts the column holds the configured value

rule_catalog.title: Normalized amount for settled gaps
rule_catalog.description: `amount_normalized` spreads the settling amount of each settled gap evenly over the months it covers: for arrears, x_q over p+1 … q; for prepay, x_p over p … q−1; for split, x_p + x_q over p … q. Each share is truncated (not rounded) to 6 decimals, and the remainder goes to the payment month: q for arrears and split, p for prepay. Each month of an uneven split (SB-11) equals its baseline b. Every other known month equals `amount`; a hole is NULL. `amount` never changes. The column is analytical only: it is never a revenue total and never drives `is_paying`, new logos or the first paid amount. The run asserts Σ `amount_normalized` = Σ `amount` per customer exactly

rule_catalog.title: Expansion and contraction proxy
rule_catalog.description: Δ = `amount_normalized`(t) − `amount_normalized`(t−1), computed only when `lifecycle_state` is `paying` in both t and t−1. `expansion_amount` = max(Δ, 0) and `contraction_amount` = max(−Δ, 0); otherwise both are 0. `amount_lag12` = `amount_normalized`(t−12), NULL before W. They are a movement proxy: a change may come from price, tax, FX or a plan change. An included row whose values are NULL under H9 is flagged `MOVEMENT_UNKNOWN`

rule_catalog.title: First-month spike
rule_catalog.description: On silver `customer`: `is_first_month_spike` = first paid amount ≥ 1.9 × next paid amount, and `first_payment_band` is `<1.9`, `1.9–3` (from 1.9, below 3) or `≥3`; both are NULL when `first_payment_ratio` is NULL. They are descriptive and never remove a logo or change a cohort. Silver keeps `first_paid_amount` and `first_payment_multiple` so a cohort's starting ARPA can be computed later (deferred with gold). A finding `FIRST_PAYMENT_UNKNOWN` is recorded for each customer with `first_payment_hole_affected` (H5)
